name: expo-app

scripts.bundle:verify: bun run check:versions && bun run bundle:ios && bun run bundle:hermes && bun run check:launch-path

//: BUILD SAFETY — three layers, because each of the first two was defeated by
the build that actually reaches the store.
1. `dependencies` says `expo-web-browser: ~15.0.11` (the SDK 54 version).
Android build 14 shipped the 56.x native module anyway and died on open:
`NoClassDefFoundError: expo.modules.kotlin.types.AnyTypeCache` at
`WebBrowserModule.definition` — a class that exists only in the SDK 56+
expo-modules-core. A version in `dependencies` is a request.
2. `overrides` (npm/pnpm) + `resolutions` (yarn/bun) pin it exactly. Build 15,
made six hours AFTER that landed, shipped the 56.x module again with the
identical trace. The cloud builder honoured neither field.
3. So the puller itself is gone. `@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk` peer-depended on
`expo-web-browser: "*"` — also `expo-blur: "*"` and `expo-router: "*"` —
and `*` matches every version ever published, so any installer that
satisfies that peer on its own terms (npm 7+ auto-installs peers) could
fetch the newest release and hoist it over ours. That is almost certainly
how the original `^56.0.5` caret arrived here. With the package removed
there is no path to `expo-web-browser` except the entry above.
`metro.config.js` carries what removing it cost.
`postinstall` runs `check:versions` on EVERY install, so an install that
resolves a wrong version fails there and then — in the cloud builder's own
log — instead of silently producing an APK that crashes on open. That is the
point: fail the build, never ship the crash.
The pins stay as defence in depth. Keep every version here EXACT and equal to
its `dependencies` entry; `check:versions` fails if they drift apart, drift
off the SDK, or if the two spellings disagree.
